It's a small Node HTTP service, five files, no framework.

1. `server.js` opens the door — it checks the `Authorization` header via `auth.js`, then hands good requests to the router.
2. `auth.js` reads bearer tokens shaped like `userId.signature`, signed with HMAC-SHA256 from `AUTH_SECRET`.
3. `routes.js` matches `method + path` against a small table: `GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`.
4. Reads go through `cache.js`, a 256-entry LRU with no expiry of its own.
5. Everything bottoms out in `store.js`, an in-memory `Map` where each record dies 15 minutes after its last write.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  server[server.js] -->|checks token| auth[auth.js]
  server -->|routes request| routes[routes.js]
  routes -->|reads| cache[cache.js]
  routes -->|writes| store[store.js]
  cache --> store
```

Writes skip the cache and go straight to the store, so a `POST /orders` won't show up on the next `GET /orders` until that cache key falls out of the LRU or the 15-minute TTL clears it. Worth knowing if you're debugging stale reads.
